key_insight: Gravity and particle inertia together control how microparticles cluster in unsteady cylinder wakes, shifting voids from leaf-like to snake-like and then nearly vertical as settling strengthens.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict and manage particle mixing, deposition, and transport in bluff-body flows such as multiphase process channels, sedimenting suspensions, and flow diagnostic setups.
method: Direct numerical simulation of particle-laden flow past a cylinder in a vertical channel.
Tested Reynolds numbers 100 and 200 with varying Stokes number, particle loading, and Froude number.
Used Voronoi tessellation and local Q-criterion to quantify clustering and wake-structure effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports Reynolds-number-dependent wake evolution and shows that St/Fr^2 governs void-shape evolution, normalized void area, and Voronoi-cell area statistics.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on DNS in an idealized cylinder wake, so extrapolation to more complex or higher-Re industrial flows should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Role of gravity on preferential clustering of microparticles in unsteady wake flows
